 Judgment
The claimant in MVC 249/2012 on the file of AMACT, Belgaum is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.
The Tribunal has held that the claimant has contributed 30% to the cause of the accident and the driver of the truck is responsible to the extent of 70%.
Accordingly, the compensation is reduced by 30%.
2. Sri Girish Yadawad, learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that the Tribunal erred in holding that the claimant is responsible for the accident to the extent of 30%.
He would further submit that accident occurred solely on account of the negligence on the part of the driver of the truck who had parked the truck on the centre of the road close to the median.
He would further submit that merely because the charge sheet is filed against the rider of the bike, it cannot be said that the rider of the bike has contributed to the accident to the extent of 30%.

The accident occurred as he was following the truck on the road and the truck driver took the vehicle to the left side and thereafter, the rider of the bike collided against the stationary vehicle which was parked on the centre of the road.
3.

Sri M K Soudagar, learned counsel appearing for the insurer would contend that that accident took place in the city and the vehicle insured by the insurer was stationed on account of the mechanical defect and there was city lights and there was no other need for the driver of the stationed vehicle to caution the public at large who are using the public road where the vehicle was stationed and he would further submit that the charge sheet is failed against the rider of the bike and no charge sheet is filed against the driver of the truck.
Under the circumstances, the Tribunal is justified in holding that the rider of the bike has contributed to the accident to the extent of 30%.
4. This Court has considered the contentions raised at the bar.
This Court has perused the sketch produced by the police along with the charge sheet.
5. In the sketch it is apparent that the trucked insured by the insurer was stationed on the middle of the road close to the median.
There is nothing on record to indicate that the vehicle was stationed because of mechanical defect.

There is again nothing on record to show that necessary precautionary measures were taken by the driver of the said truck to caution the public who were using the said road to the effect that the vehicle is stationed on the road on account of the mechanical defect.
This being the position, it is said that the facts speak for themselves.
The fact that truck was stationed on the middle of the road is not disputed.
This Court is of the view that the tribunal erred in holding that the rider of the bike has contributed to the accident to the extent of 30%.
6. It has also to be noted that the driver of the truck is not examined to show that the vehicle was stationed on account of mechanical defect.

This being the position, this Court considering the other evidence on record particularly the evidence of the claimant who was an eye witness to the accident is of the view that 10% liability is to be fastened on the rider of the bike.

sentences.text: As far as the claim for enhancement of compensation under various heads claimed in the appeal memo, this Court has considered the award of compensation by the Tribunal on various heads.
It is noticed that compensation of Rs.50,000/- is awarded towards pain and suffering.
Sri .Girish Yadawad submits that the appellant has suffered 8 fractures and that being the case the compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the above said head is inadequate.
Sri .M.K.Soudagar submits that facial injuries do not cause much pain and as such Rs.50,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is just and fair compensation.
8. This Court has also noticed that no compensation is awarded under the head of loss of amenities in life.
Sri.Girish Yadawad submits that on account of the injuries sustained by the claimant to the jaw of the petitioner has to endeavor the discomfort for the rest of his life while chewing hard materials.
Sri .M.K.Soudagar submits that the Tribunal is not justified in awarding compensation under the said head since the same would not result into any loss of amenities.
9. This Court has considered the contentions raised at the bar.

Taking into consideration the claimant has suffered 8 fractures and injury to the jaw and also considering the fact that out of 8 fractures 6 fracture are on face and jaw, this Court is of the view that Rs.35,000/- is to be awarded under the head of loss of amenities and considering the fact that 8 fractures are sustained by the claimant, compensation under the head, pain and suffering is to be enhanced by another Rs.10,000/-.
In all, enhanced compensation of Rs.45,000/- is awarded under the aforementioned two heads.
10. As far as liability is concerned, this Court has already held that the claimant has contributed to the extent of only 10%.
11. Thus, the enhanced compensation shall carry 6% interest and the same shall be deposited before the Tribunal within six weeks from today.
12. Appeal is allowed in part and the judgment and award of the Tribunal are modified as indicated above.

13. Application seeking production of additional document is not taken into consideration as the documents are pertaining to some medical bills which the claimant claims to have incurred during the pendency of appeal.
Hence, the said application is dismissed.
